newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan mulls privatisation of troubled nuclear firm.
newsitem.headline: Japan mulls privatisation of troubled nuclear firm.

text.p: The head of Japan's state-run nuclear processing company, under fire for delayed and deceptive reporting of a series of accidents, told parliament on Tuesday the firm was discussing privatising its two main functions.

The Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC) was negotiating turning its uranium enrichment and nuclear fuel reprocessing operations to the private sector, PNC president Toshiyuki Kondo said.

The measures are part of a sweeping restructuring of the company which has admitted it filed a false report on Japan's worst-ever nuclear accident last month and failed to report nearly 20 radiation leaks in the past five years.

PNC was negotiating the transfer of its uranium enrichment operation to Japan Nuclear Fuel Ltd, a private entity owned mainly by Japan's nine major electric power companies, Kondo told a parliamentary committee.
A fire and explosion on March 11 at PNC's nuclear reprocessing plant in Tokaimura, on the Pacific coast 100 km (60 miles) northeast of Tokyo, exposed 37 workers to low-level radiation.
PNC admitted earlier this month that it had falsified a report on the March accident, incorrectly saying staff had visually confirmed that a fire had been extinguished at a nuclear waste facility.
In fact, no staff had confirmed that the fire had been put out. The fire later flared up and triggered the explosion.
The government's Science and Technology Agency responded to the revelations by filing a criminal complaint against the firm, which it founded and oversees.
Pursuing the complaint, police have questioned PNC officials and media reports said investigators would raid PNC's Tokyo headquarters as early as Wednesday.

Two days before the science agency filed its complaint, PNC was forced to shut down an advanced thermal reactor called Fugen in western Japan after it had waited 30 hours before reporting a radiation leak which exposed 11 workers to low-level radiation.

PNC subsequently acknowledged it had not reported 18 separate radiation leaks at the 18-year-old Fugen reactor since 1992, saying the amount of leaked radiation was below the level at which they were legally required to do so.
On Tuesday, an opposition-sponsored no-confidence motion against Science and Technology Agency chief Riichiro Chikaoka over PNC's recent troubles was defeated in the Lower House of Parliament.
